Another huge change that’s long overdue is the resolution and full screen viewing of photos. Come on already. I add on to my review the number of restrictions Instagram automatically applies to peoples accounts. Hi, I have non epileptic seizures (seizures that mimic epileptic seizures without sending electrical currents through the brain and instead is caused by something functional in the brain). Triggers for these seizures can include ✨strobe lights✨. Lately I have been coming across more and more videos that include strobe lights without the use of flash warnings and I usually comment to politely ask to add a warning however in some cases comments will be disabled or the creator with refuse to put a warning. I know that this isn’t Instagrams fault but I have some ideas to help reduce the risk of seizures from videos containing strobe. 

I feel as if Instagram should add a feature to report videos containing flash to hide the video from photosensitive viewers much like the warnings used for graphic material. This can help protect ourselves from future seizures and flair ups. I know that some people think this might be a dumb request “there aren’t warnings in the real world” “toughen up and get over it” but the thing is that this IS the real world, we can’t get over it because that’s just our life. For some people no flash warnings can be a matter between life or death. You’re playing with peoples lives here. People with seizures have gone through so much trauma, experiencing seizures are terrifying no matter how many you may get. 

Please consider this feature, I’ve had enough of this, and I am so tired. This is so important to us

My biggest issue with Instagram lately is their application of community guidelines. They seem very inconsistent and biased- strictly following the guidelines with some content but not other similar content, especially when it comes to “political” content... this can greatly affect what content you are allowed to see, comment on, post and share. The “fact check” feature also seems to be bias on particular things.

Reporting content and comments that are not appropriate, especially things regarding bullying and discrimination, or fake/scam accounts pretending to be other people, seems to do very little most of the time, and nothing is usually done about the post/comment you report- only suggesting you block the person you have reported, which doesn’t always fix the issue. The process for reporting things like people stealing your content (copyright infringement) and/or invading your privacy, while generally more effective and successful than the conventional way of reporting things, is also much more difficult- it’s hard to find where and how to send reports directly this way, and is more time consuming. 

The live streams always seem to be glitchy and troublesome, both for the host of the lives and the viewers. Editing reels and stories can also be a pain, with additional features not always loading, things being out of time after uploading, sound playing but the video being frozen, or the app crashing all together and randomly shutting down.

I have always loved the idea of Instagram. I think the concept, what they have done in the social media sphere is amazing but I think there are ways we could make social media “healthier”. It can be so hard for some people to have social media and not get sucked into a never ending rabbit hole. The results can be that people end up not living their life because hours and hours are spent scrolling, addicted to their phone. I understand social media is a large part of how a lot of people make their income but for many, it is a way to keep in touch with friends and search up new friends, be artistic, post life updates, message and so on. 

I would love to see a function on Instagram in the settings that allows the user (or even parents of kids) to disable the discovery page function. I think it would prevent the endless scrolling you can get sucked into. It would still allow you to search for accounts and friends but you’re not exposed to everything and everyone the algorithm sends your way. I think it would make a huge difference to some users experience on the app, in a positive way. I know it’s something I would benefit from personally and not cause me to delete the app all the time.

What was good or useful about Instagram is gradually whittled away until all social media platforms are the same, partitioning each individual into a separate box with a tailored stream of content designed to retain engagement and simulate an idea of community connection.
Updates are pushed asynchronously, which means that none of your friends have that new bad feature you just got, so they don’t understand what you’re complaining about, until one day you all do and it’s just how it works now.
I’ve noticed the app withholds the dopamine hit from seeing the red dot that indicates ppl have liked your posts until you’ve checked the app a couple times that day already; if you check it earlier, the likes are there, but really, that validation is just another tool in the quest to retain as much of your attention as possible.
Even beyond theses criticisms, for an image-centric platform, Instagram stores very low quality jpeg images, with some kind of automatic sharpen/contrast filter that makes non-photographic images look particularly bad.
Think critically about how you engage with this app, and pay attention to how the incremental changes make you feel. When you add them together, do you like where this platform is going?

This latest Instagram update, where they’ve changed the ratio and presentation of posts on your profile page, is an absolute eyesore. What was once a clean, cohesive grid of beautifully curated posts now feels clunky and disjointed. The aesthetic flow of a profile—the very thing Instagram was built on—is completely ruined.

Why on earth would they mess with the post display ratio? People spend hours, if not days, planning their grids to look visually appealing, and now all that effort is wasted. Photos are cropped awkwardly, reels dominate the page in an unbalanced way, and the layout feels cluttered and chaotic. It’s like they’ve forgotten that a significant portion of users are creators who care about how their content looks on their profile.

Not to mention, it makes scrolling through someone’s profile less enjoyable. The uniformity of the grid was what made it so satisfying, and now it’s just frustrating to look at. This feels like a classic case of “fixing something that wasn’t broken.” Instead of addressing actual issues users have—like giving us chronological feeds or better control over algorithmic recommendations—they decided to break the one thing that consistently worked.

Instagram, please listen to your users for once. Roll this back before you alienate the people who care about curating content on your platform. The grid was iconic—stop ruining what makes Instagram, Instagram.

Despite what appears to be a minor initial wave of criticism, the concept of removing likes is a well-considered one.

It upsets me that commenters below have shared sentiments to the effect of: “I miss the popularity contest” and “what’s the point of posting anymore.” 

Social media and more generally, communication, should ideally be valued by what is being said, rather than the individual who is saying it. It is telling (and perhaps alarming) that some feel there is no purpose to sharing the things we enjoy without a likes system. This post is not to scrutinise those who appreciate validation and positive feedback, which is something we are all guilty of, in part. To those who do find this essential, why is the fact that you can view how many likes your own post received insufficient? Is there some conceited pleasure to derive from surpassing others in this way?

I hope this update encourages us all to share more of what we love, free of fear, free of judgment and free of vanity.

I understand why you might have concerns about Instagram. Like many social media platforms, it has both positive and negative aspects.

On the positive side, Instagram offers a way for people to connect with others, share experiences, and showcase creativity. It can also be an important tool for businesses, artists, and influencers to reach large audiences.

However, there are several criticisms:
	1.	Mental Health Impact: Constant exposure to curated, often unrealistic images can lead to body image issues, low self-esteem, and anxiety. Comparing oneself to others online can sometimes create feelings of inadequacy.
	2.	Addiction and Time Waste: Instagram, like other social media platforms, can be highly addictive. The endless scrolling, notifications, and dopamine hits from likes or comments can lead to overuse and distraction from more meaningful activities.
	3.	Privacy Concerns: Instagram collects a lot of data from its users, raising concerns about privacy and data security.
	4.	Echo Chambers: The algorithm tends to reinforce your existing interests and biases, potentially limiting exposure to diverse perspectives.
